answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates via bounded random walks, so influence depends on transition mass rather than raw identities. An adversarial sybil cluster separated by a sparse external cut of conductance φ receives limited walk flow; spectral mixing and min-cut transitivity bounds therefore cap its aggregate voting weight, which declines as φ shrinks. Thus an ivory oasis of colluding nodes cannot amplify a delta-sized bridge into majority power.
